s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement
salient_findings: Ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
key_facts: 18-year-old man
6 months of fluctuating lower-limb weakness
Initial episode of leg weakness resolved over 30 minutes
Asymptomatic for 4 months
Developed ascending spastic weakness over 3 months
Urinary retention requiring a Foley catheter
One month of constipation
No trauma, fever, steroid or other drug intake, or infections
Normal routine hematological and biochemical tests
Normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Unremarkable plain radiographs of the spine
Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 on MRI

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 on MRI, suggestive of fat

shortlist.label: Spinal cord tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Spinal cord tumor possibility with fluctuating weakness and spinal mass

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Spinal mass with potential for infection, although no fever or infection reported

shortlist.label: Multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuating course of lower limb weakness, although less likely given spinal mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 that is homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI sequences, suggestive of fat, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: The MRI characteristics do not suggest a tumor, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with compression by a fatty mass.

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Ependymomas are typically intramedullary spinal cord tumors and do not match the epidural location of the mass described.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: The absence of fever, infection, or elevated inflammatory markers, along with the MRI appearance suggestive of fat, makes an abscess unlikely.

rejected.label: Multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the presence of a specific epidural mass on MRI do not align with the typical diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, which usually involves more widespread and multifocal lesions in the central nervous system.
